items.title: The Steelers have named Mason Rudolph their starter for Week 12 against the Broncos.
items.text: The news of Aaron Rodgers’ benching and Rudolph’s sudden promotion came in an 11:10 PM ET Tuesday evening press release. Normal stuff. While we wait for the next shoe to drop on the “Rodgers situation,” we can begin evaluating the “Rudolph development.” In short: Not much will change, though Rodgers’ recent immobility and subsequent inaccuracy had reached a boiling point. Rudolph will oversee an attack that figures to make a sudden swerve to the run, though the 31-year-old with 742 career pass attempts should be able to keep a wideout or two afloat in deeper fantasy leagues. items.title: The Steelers have announced they are benching Aaron Rodgers, with Mason Rudolph named the starter for Week 12 against the Broncos.
items.text: 42-year-old Rodgers’ play had taken a sudden, dramatic turn for the worst of late, but it’s still a stunning announcement, especially since it came via a terse team statement. It also comes one day after coach Mike McCarthy claimed he was not considering turning to one of his myriad other QB options (the team also has second-year pro Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar on the 53-man roster). Other information is scarce, except for the statement including Rodgers would be inactive for the Friday afternoon contest. items.title: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports there have “not been a lot of talks about an extension in-season” for Bryce Young.
items.text: Wolfe adds that Young and the Panthers are “on the same page for an offseason contract.” Young started out strong this season before a three-turnover loss to the Buccaneers in Week 7. The Panthers are still in first place atop the NFC South with a 5-5 record and a second bout with the Bucs on the horizon for Week 12. Young’s extension chances were highly reliant on his play this season but the Panthers need to see more before committing to the 25-year-old quarterback. items.title: Alex Highsmith (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
items.text: Highsmith suffered an ankle injury in Week 11 and starts out the week not practicing. He was wearing an ankle brace in the team facility on Tuesday and head coach Mike McCarthy said it will be “tough” for Highsmith to play in a shortened Week 12 where the Steelers play the Broncos on Friday. Highsmith is trending in the wrong direction this week, but his ankle issue does not seem to be a major injury. - Aditya Fuldeore

items.title: Quinyon Mitchell (hamstring) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
items.text: Eagles DC Vic Fangio said today he believed Mitchell would be able to go, and it seems like he’s trending in the right direction after hitting the practice field today. It would certainly help anyone facing CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens out this week if Mitchell were able to go. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Dallas Goedert (shin) practiced in full on Tuesday.
items.text: That makes us feel pretty confident that he’ll suit up for Thanksgiving’s game against the Cowboys after a limited session on Monday. The Eagles’ passing game is in pretty rough shape with Joe Milton under center, but Dallas’ issues invite a TE1-capable game script for Goedert if the Eagles can take advantage of it. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Will Shipley (foot/illness) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
items.text: With the news that Saquon Barkley is practicing in full, Shipley’s waiver wire appeal has downgraded drastically. He’s a reasonable stash and little more at this point in 12-team leagues. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Saquon Barkley (neck/illness) practiced in full on Tuesday.
items.text: It’s an upgrade over his limited session on Monday. Barkley told reporters after Sunday’s game that he doesn’t think he’ll ever get to 100 percent again for the rest of the season, saying “That’s not how football works.” But it seems like he’s at least “football healthy” enough to go against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Pat Bryant (ankle) is practicing in full for Denver’s Week 12 game against the Steelers.
items.text: Bryant survived an injury scare on Sunday and this confirms that he should be in a good place to play on Friday. He took over as Denver’s No. 2 receiver against the Raiders, out-targeting Courtland Sutton 4-2, but wasn’t able to make much fantasy hay of the increased workload. Pittsburgh should be another game that mostly sees Bryant as a FLEX play at best. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Free agent WR Brandon Aiyuk will visit the Commanders on Wednesday.
items.text: Aiyuk’s last two days have gone pretty much exactly how you would have expected after the 49ers finally released him. He’ll likely sign with the Commanders practice squad officially tomorrow. - Rivers McCown
